headline: Shoring Up Trust in Streaming, Enterprise Auth, and Tool-Calling
body:
This quarter's work targets three areas that shape whether developers and enterprises can rely on our platform for production agent workloads: streaming reliability, enterprise-grade authentication, and tool-calling robustness.

First priority, landing in Q1, is fixing core streaming reliability. Today, streaming breaks or silently falls back to non-streamed behavior across several common scenarios - provider proxies, structured output, selective streaming controls, and agent/graph execution - which undermines confidence in a capability that is central to how developers build with our product. Alongside this, we're closing an enterprise adoption gap: teams that require custom certificate-based authentication or secure proxy access currently cannot connect reliably, and a security validation gap could let requests reach untrusted hosts. Both of these Q1 workstreams are similarly sized and similarly impactful, addressing core trust and enterprise-readiness issues respectively.

Following in Q2, we'll harden the tool-calling pipeline that underlies agent products. This includes making sure human-in-the-loop rejections are always honored (a safety-critical gap today), improving reliability when tool-call data is malformed, and improving observability and error-handling consistency for developers building multi-tool agents. Sequencing this after the Q1 work lets us first stabilize the foundational streaming and auth layers that agents depend on.

Across all three areas, the underlying evidence is a mix of a few high-frequency, high-confidence problems and several lower-frequency individual reports, so we are prioritizing based on severity and strategic importance (enterprise unblocking, safety-critical gaps) rather than volume alone.
call_to_action: Requesting endorsement of the proposed sequencing: streaming reliability and enterprise auth/transport security in Q1, followed by tool-calling pipeline hardening in Q2.

key_claims.text: Streaming breaks or silently falls back to non-streamed behavior across provider proxies, structured output, selective streaming controls, and agent/graph execution.
Streaming reliability work is scheduled for Q1.
Enterprise teams cannot reliably configure custom certificate-based authentication (mTLS) or secure proxy access today.
A security validation gap could allow SSRF/allowlist bypass via environment-based auth checks, letting requests reach untrusted hosts.
Enterprise auth and transport security work is scheduled for Q1.
Tool-calling pipeline hardening is scheduled for Q2 and does not depend on the Q1 workstreams.
Human-in-the-loop tool-call rejection is not reliably enforced today, meaning a rejected tool call can still be executed.
Tool-calling work also addresses malformed/fragmented tool-call payload handling, observability of parallel tool calls, and inconsistent error-handling across code paths.
Streaming, authentication, and tool-calling issues are each backed by a mix of a few higher-frequency problems and several individual (frequency of 1-2) reports.
